subject: 2026 Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponement
title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed: New date is Saturday, Nov. 28
answer: The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed from Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26, 2026, to Saturday, Nov. 28, because a coastal storm was forecast to bring heavy rain and gusts above 60 mph to New York City. It is the first time in the parade's history that weather has pushed it to another day.
in_the_news: Millions of families planned their Thanksgiving morning around the 100th parade, and many tuned in to NBC on Thursday expecting it live. The new Saturday date, route and broadcast details are what viewers and spectators now need.
body:
The decision was made Wednesday afternoon, Nov. 25, after close consultation between Macy's, New York City and NBC, according to The Weather Channel and Forbes. Macy's said the safety of participants and spectators was its top priority. The National Weather Service had issued a high wind warning for the city from 10 a.m. Thursday through late Thursday night, with sustained winds of 25 to 35 mph and gusts above 60 mph. That is far beyond the city's limit for giant balloons: they cannot fly at full height when sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts exceed 34 mph. Crews had already begun inflating balloons on Wednesday and had to deflate them.

The parade will now step off at 8:30 a.m. ET on Saturday and run until about noon, CBS New York reported. The roughly 2.5-mile route is unchanged: it starts at West 76th Street and Central Park West, turns onto West 59th Street, heads down Sixth Avenue and ends at Macy's Herald Square on West 34th Street. The lineup includes 28 floats, dozens of giant balloons, five "balloonicles," nine marching bands and a long list of performers, and it still ends with Santa Claus, which traditionally opens the holiday shopping season.

A century of weather at the parade: the first parade marched in 1924. It was canceled in 1942, 1943 and 1944 during World War II. In 1971, wind and rain kept every giant balloon on the ground, though floats and bands still marched — the only time the whole balloon lineup was grounded. In 1997, a wind-blown balloon struck a lamppost and injured a spectator, which led to today's 23 mph and 34 mph wind limits. Until 2026, bad weather had changed how the parade looked, but never the day it took place.

What it means for you: if you plan to watch in person, spectators may line up from 6 a.m. Saturday along Central Park West between West 75th and West 61st streets, and Sixth Avenue from West 59th to West 38th streets is a popular viewing area. Dress for a chilly morning: the Saturday forecast calls for highs in the low 50s with gusts of about 20 mph, below the balloon limit. At home, the parade airs live on NBC and streams on Peacock, with a Spanish-language broadcast on Telemundo. The MTA and the city's transportation department said they would announce Saturday transit changes and street closures.

faq.q: What is NBC showing instead of the parade on Thanksgiving?
faq.a: Forbes reported that NBC and Peacock aired an encore of the 2025 parade on Thanksgiving morning, starting at 8:30 a.m. The live 2026 parade moves to Saturday, Nov. 28.

faq.q: What time does the rescheduled parade start?
faq.a: 8:30 a.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 28, 2026 (7:30 a.m. PT on NBC), and it is expected to end around noon.

faq.q: Will the giant balloons fly on Saturday?
faq.a: They are expected to. Forecast gusts for Saturday morning are around 20 to 25 mph, below the 34 mph gust limit, but officials make the final call on parade day.

faq.q: Has the Macy's parade ever been canceled before?
faq.a: Yes, but not for weather. It was canceled from 1942 to 1944 during World War II. The 2026 postponement is the first time weather has moved it to a different day.
